newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa has irregular heartbeat.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa has irregular heartbeat.

text.p: Mother Teresa briefly had irregular heartbeats on Sunday night, four days after she had been given a mild electric shock to correct her heart's erratic rhythm, an official at an Indian clinic said on Monday.

"She had the problem of irregular heartbeats last night," a spokesman for Calcutta's B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre, where the 86-year-old Roman Catholic nun is being treated, told Reuters. The problem had lasted only a few minutes, he added.

A regular medical update on Mother Teresa's condition said: "She is stable, but her heartbeat is irregular. She had good sleep at night. She had morning tea around 0700 hours (0130 GMT) and her prayer around 0800 hours."
Mother Teresa had surgery last month to clear two blocked coronary arteries. Her recovery was delayed by her irregular heart rhythm and long-standing lung and kidney problems.
Doctors who corrected the irregular heartbeat by administering a mild electric shock on Wednesday had said the procedure was a success.
The 1979 Nobel peace prize winner is revered by thousands all over the world for her lifelong devotion to the poor, the sick and the dying.
